transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I feel like I’ve lost all interest in teaching and the activities I used to enjoy, and I can’t seem to care about anything the way I used to. Everything just feels completely flat, and I can't find any motivation or joy in the things that used to make me happy.
How long have you been feeling this way? Also, did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or change in your life?

These feelings have been building and pretty constant for about a year and a half now. It really started after I took on a lot of extra responsibilities at my school, including an advanced STEM track and managing multiple clubs. At the same time, the district rolled out a highly stressful new evaluation system that put immense pressure on us.
Along with this loss of interest, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns, appetite, or overall energy levels during this time?

Yes, I'm completely exhausted all the time; I lie awake for hours with my mind racing about work, wake up around 4 or 5 a.m., and no amount of rest makes me feel less drained. I've also lost my appetite and often go the whole school day on just coffee, so my clothes have started fitting much looser. Even simple things like folding laundry feel like climbing a mountain now.
During this past year and a half, have you also been struggling with feelings of worthlessness, or finding yourself feeling excessively guilty about things?

Yes, I feel that way constantly. Whenever I miss a deadline or a student's scores dip, I spiral into thinking I'm a terrible teacher and a bad wife who is letting everyone down. I constantly replay mistakes from years ago, convinced that I don't deserve my job or the support people give me.
Before these past 18 months, did you have a long history of feeling generally low, sad, or mildly depressed for most of the day, perhaps going back several years?
No, I don't recall ever having those feelings or any history of depression before this recent period. I used to be very active, organized, and genuinely happy with my life and career.
When you are feeling this down and overwhelmed, have you had any thoughts of death, or felt that you would be better off dead?

Yes, especially at night when I'm feeling so overwhelmed by failing at work and home, I catch myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up or got into an accident. I don't have any plan to actually do anything, but the idea of just not being here anymore sometimes feels like a relief.
Have you ever experienced periods lasting several days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, hyperactive, or needing very little sleep without feeling tired?
No, I’ve never felt that way at all. My energy has been consistently very low, and I just feel completely exhausted and drained. I’ve never had periods where I felt hyperactive or didn't need sleep.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate, focus on your teaching, or make everyday decisions during this time?

Yes, my concentration and decision-making have suffered significantly. I used to be incredibly organized, but now my brain feels so foggy that I find myself rereading a single email three times, zoning out while grading, or getting completely stuck on simple decisions like which unit to teach next.
Have you recently been diagnosed with any medical conditions, like thyroid problems, or started any new medications that could be contributing to your fatigue and low mood?
No, I haven't been diagnosed with any other medical conditions, and my thyroid is fine as far as I know. I'm also not currently taking any new medications.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with an 18-month history of a severe, continuous depressive episode characterized by three core symptoms (depressed mood/flat affect, marked anhedonia, and severe fatigue/loss of energy) and five additional symptoms (early-morning insomnia, appetite/weight loss, excessive guilt and feelings of worthlessness, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, and passive suicidal ideation). The onset was triggered by significant work-related psychosocial stressors. There is no prior history of manic, hypomanic, or chronic low-grade depressive symptoms (dysthymia), and medical/substance-induced etiologies have been ruled out.
